detail: People are 65% more likely to hit a goal after committing to someone; with a deadline + regular progress sharing, success rises up to ~95%.
Accountability research finds the partner should be a friend - exactly what a WhatsApp family/friends group is, unlike a public feed of strangers.
WhatsApp's ~83% daily/monthly ratio makes it the highest-frequency retention surface in Meta's portfolio - a progress ping lands daily.
A group post carries relational weight and a ~98% open rate; an in-app feed update is passive by comparison.
Publicly announcing an identity goal can create a 'premature sense of completion' that REDUCES follow-through - a real risk for any 'share your goal' feature.
Automated 'X posted an update' pings into already-busy group chats (half of 150B daily messages) risk annoyance and muting.
WhatsApp is closed and encrypted - it can lift retention but does nothing for acquisition; there is no Explore-style growth loop here.
Only ~100M US monthly users (~3% of global). In a US-first launch the WhatsApp lever is weak; its power is in India/Brazil/Indonesia.
The whole mechanic hinges on opt-in rates; if few users connect a group, the retention multiplier never materializes.
Journeys' ongoing-update cadence sidesteps the Gollwitzer trap: it shares incremental progress, not a one-time identity declaration - which is the accountability-positive pattern.
Keep group pings per-update, opt-in, and trivially mutable to avoid fatigue - the difference between a welcome nudge and a reason to leave the group.

factor: Treat as retention and gate it
detail: Measure opt-in rate and its retention lift; deprioritize if it doesn't move retention - exactly the rollout's Phase 2 gate.
